breakdown.desc: FLHSMV rated it Definitely/Highly Likely an e-bike crash; the LLM named an e-scooter.
FLHSMV Definitely; the LLM said regular bicycle, but the property-damage field says electric bicycle.
FLHSMV rated Likely or higher; the LLM's rules sent it to Other (motorcycle-type, unclear or missing device, and so on).
FLHSMV rated Likely or higher; the LLM said regular bicycle and the property field does not explain it.
FLHSMV rated Less/Not Likely; the LLM found an e-bike or e-scooter.

rules.definition: "Scooter" on its own with no power wording, brand, posture or speed, or a "stand-up scooter" with no motor/electric wording (could be a kick scooter) -> Other.
No device named at all (pedestrian only, no vehicle described, or only a bike lane or path mentioned) -> Other.
"Motorized scooter" or "motor scooter" on its own (no standing posture, brand or speed of 15 mph or more), or a seated motorized scooter (could be a gas moped) -> Other.
Electric devices that are neither e-bike nor e-scooter (electric unicycle, hoverboard, electric or motorized skateboard, motorized wheelchair, toy bike, electric dirt bike) -> Other.
Gas-powered or moped-class devices (moped, motorcycle, minibike, "cc", "engine", Vespa and similar) -> Other.
Two or more device classes in the same narrative (for example e-bike and e-scooter, or scooter and bicycle) -> Other.
Human-power override: wording such as foot powered, manual, non-motorized or non-electric -> Other, even if a brand name appears.
Slash ambiguity such as "ebike/escooter" or "bicycle/scooter" -> Other.
Catch-all for ambiguous or unidentifiable devices ("bike" alone with power clues, "scooter" alone, pedestrian only, skateboard, ATV, go-kart, no device named, and similar) -> Other.
Wheel-count override: a 3- or 4-wheel scooter -> Other.
Electric moped (a separate Florida vehicle class, not an e-bike) -> Other.
"Motorized bicycle" with gas evidence, or on its own (power type unknown) -> Other.

flhsmv_defs.label: Definitely
flhsmv_defs.definition: The crash report definitely involves an E-Bike or E-Scooter. Variations of the two are explicitly mentioned in the Narrative or Property Damage fields.

flhsmv_defs.label: Highly Likely
flhsmv_defs.definition: Highly likely to involve an E-Bike or E-Scooter. Key words such as "Electric", "Bike" and "Scooter" are used in conjunction with each other multiple times in the Narrative or Property Damage fields.

flhsmv_defs.label: Likely
flhsmv_defs.definition: Possibly contains an e-bike or e-scooter. Key words such as "Electric" and "Motorized" appear once.

flhsmv_defs.label: Less Likely
flhsmv_defs.definition: A "Bike" or "Scooter" is mentioned, but there is no explicit reference to motorization.

flhsmv_defs.label: Not Likely
flhsmv_defs.definition: No key words are referenced, but property damage is reported. Some reports may have slipped by.

flhsmv_defs.label: Not Enough Information
flhsmv_defs.definition: No key words are referenced and no property damage is reported, so there is not enough information to categorize.

bottom_line: The LLM and FLHSMV tell broadly the same story, and most differences trace back to how each is defined. FLHSMV's ratings are keyword-based ("electric", "bike", "scooter", "motorized"), look at both the narrative and the property-damage field, and group e-bikes and e-scooters together. The LLM reads only the narrative and needs explicit evidence of both the device and its electric power before it will say e-bike or e-scooter. So when the LLM does name one, FLHSMV had already rated it likely 99.7% of the time. The gaps come from three places: the LLM was never shown the property-damage column, where officers often wrote "electric bicycle" (696 reports); the LLM's rules deliberately send vague wording (a bare "scooter" or "bike", "motorized scooter" alone, several devices at once, no device) to "Other" where FLHSMV's keywords gave a likely rating (1,754 reports); and the LLM separates e-scooters from e-bikes while FLHSMV does not (4,084 reports, a disagreement only under the strict view). A small group (28) went the other way: FLHSMV rated them unlikely, yet the narrative describes an e-bike or e-scooter. Neither source is treated as the final truth; settling the disputed cases would take a human review.

insights.title: When the LLM spots an e-bike or e-scooter, FLHSMV almost always agrees
insights.text: Of every 9,434 reports the LLM called an e-bike or e-scooter, FLHSMV had rated all but a handful as at least "Likely". So the LLM's positive calls are very dependable. Its weakness is the other direction: it recovers about 78.3% of the reports FLHSMV rated likely, because it is stricter about what counts.
insights.evidence: Precision 99.7%, recall 78.3%, F1 87.7% (FLHSMV treated as the reference).

insights.title: Much of the "disagreement" is a difference in definition, not a mistake
insights.text: FLHSMV's own rating definition covers "an E-Bike or E-Scooter" together, so the LLM's e-scooter calls are consistent with it. The LLM keeps them separate, following the Florida legal split (an e-bike has pedals and a motor; an e-scooter has no pedals). That is why the comparison jumps from 48.8% (strict, only LLM E-bike counts) to 80.1% (lenient, E-bike or E-scooter counts). The lenient figure is the like-for-like one. In 30% of these cases FLHSMV's own property-damage field also says "scooter".
insights.evidence: 4,084 reports FLHSMV rated Definitely/Highly Likely that the LLM called E-scooter; 1,238 mention a scooter in the property-damage field.

insights.title: The LLM was blind to a column that held the answer
insights.text: The LLM read the crash narrative but was not given the property-damage field (TYPE_PROPERTY_DAMAGE). In 696 reports FLHSMV rated the crash "Definitely" an e-bike, the narrative did not mention a motor (true for 694 of them), and the property field said things like "electric bicycle". The LLM called these regular bicycles with high confidence. Here FLHSMV is right and the LLM simply lacked the information. Giving the LLM that column would likely lift agreement to about 85.4%.
insights.evidence: 696 reports; 694 of them say the narrative mentions no power source; best case agreement 80.1% to about 85.4%.

insights.title: FLHSMV's "Likely" rating is loose; its top two ratings are solid
insights.text: The LLM confirms most "Highly Likely" reports (89.1%) and, once the blind spot is credited, most "Definitely" reports (89.9%). "Likely" is different: the LLM confirms only 9.9% and calls 77% of them "Other". FLHSMV defines "Likely" as keywords such as "electric" or "motorized" appearing just once, a weaker standard than the LLM's requirement for explicit evidence of both the device and its electric power. Counting "Likely" as a yes therefore adds many reports that are questionable.
insights.evidence: Share the LLM confirms: Definitely 76.4% (89.9% with blind spot credited), Highly Likely 89.1%, Likely 9.9%.

insights.title: Where the LLM says "Other", it is usually following a rule not to guess
insights.text: For 1,754 reports FLHSMV rated likely but the LLM said "Other". The LLM's prompt tells it to answer "Other" whenever the device or its power type is unclear: a bare "scooter" or "bike", "motorized scooter" on its own (it could be gas-powered), several devices in one report, or no device at all. About 78% fall under just three of those rules. FLHSMV's keyword criteria, by contrast, can reach a likely rating from a single "motorized" or "electric". Keyword matching can also pick up incidental mentions, for example 2 reports where the narrative mentions a scooter lift or carrier on a vehicle. In many of these FLHSMV may be right and the LLM too cautious, but the data cannot say which; a human review of a sample would settle it.
insights.evidence: 1,754 reports (14.6% of FLHSMV positives); see the rule table.

insights.title: FLHSMV occasionally rates a real e-bike as unlikely
insights.text: In 28 reports FLHSMV said "Less Likely" or "Not Likely", yet the narrative describes an e-bike (25) or e-scooter (3). Almost all (26 of 28) sit in the regular-bike file. That is only 2.3% of everything FLHSMV rated unlikely, so FLHSMV's low ratings are mostly reliable, but the LLM could help catch the few it misses.

insights.title: The two sources disagree more for some agencies than others
insights.text: Among agencies with at least 100 FLHSMV-positive reports, the LLM disagrees most often for Florida Highway Patrol (46.6%), Hollywood Police Department (41.4%) and Jacksonville Sheriff's Office (37.0%), and least for Key West Police Department (5.5%). Part of the gap is where an agency records "electric": for Florida Highway Patrol, 40% of its disagreements are the property-field blind spot, which would shrink its rate from 46.6% to about 27.9%.
insights.evidence: Overall, the LLM disagrees with 21.7% of FLHSMV-positive reports.

insights.title: The LLM sounds equally sure when it is right and when it lacks information
insights.text: Its self-reported confidence is about 0.95 for Bicyclist, E-bike and E-scooter, and lower (0.77) for "Other", so low confidence does point to ambiguous reports. But it cannot catch the blind spot: those 696 reports were all labeled at 0.95. Confidence is a useful flag for "Other", not a safety net.
insights.evidence: Mean confidence: Bicyclist 0.95, E-bike 0.95, E-scooter 0.95, Other 0.77.

insights.title: The share of FLHSMV-positive reports the LLM confirms has risen over time
insights.text: In the e-bike file, the LLM confirmed 73.5% of FLHSMV-positive reports in 2023 Q1 and 83.7% in 2026 Q2 (a partial quarter), with a low of 70.0% in 2023 Q3. The data cannot say why: narratives may have become more explicit, FLHSMV coding may have changed, or the mix of e-scooters may have shifted.

misc.text: Of 20,769 unique REPORT_NUMBERs (15,953 in the e-bike file, 4,816 in the regular-bike file, no overlap), 13,248 (63.8%) were found in the FLHSMV files and 7,521 (36.2%) were not. Match rate is 75.3% for the e-bike file and 25.7% for the regular-bike file.

The unmatched IDs are clean 8-digit numbers that simply do not appear in the FLHSMV files, so this is not a formatting problem. They cluster in two places: IDs starting with 80 to 90 (4,326 unmatched, only 13.2% found) and IDs starting with 21 to 24 (1,530 unmatched, 13.3% found), against 88.1% found for IDs starting with 25 to 28. The FLHSMV records that did match were loaded between 2023-01-01 and 2026-05-07, so crashes outside that window could be absent. Whether the two sources cover different years cannot be tested from this workbook, because unmatched rows carry no FLHSMV date. The cause is therefore not confirmed; rerunning the build script with power_bi_export.csv adds a crash-year check.

misc.theme: Unmatched reports that still look like e-bikes
misc.text: Among the 7,521 unmatched IDs, 2,465 (32.8%) are ones the LLM called E-bike or E-scooter. These crashes exist in the LLM data but cannot be compared with FLHSMV. The FLHSMV files may be a partial extract, so confirm before calling these FLHSMV omissions.

The two files are almost pure slices of the FLHSMV rating. In the e-bike file, 12,007 of 12,009 matched IDs are FLHSMV-positive; in the regular-bike file, 1,238 of 1,239 are FLHSMV-negative. Agreement is 78.3% in the first and 97.8% in the second, and the 80.1% headline blends them. These numbers describe this sample, not all Florida e-bike crashes.

The FLHSMV files repeat some REPORT_NUMBERs (for example a crash with both an L and a U form). 964 matched IDs have more than one row (909 have both an L and a U form), and 107 of them carry different FLHSMV ratings. The workbook's Joined sheets keep every row (17,061 and 4,946 rows; 1,238 extra). Everything on this tab uses one row per ID, keeping the highest FLHSMV rating.
Agreement is similar across FLHSMV form types: 80.2% for L, 80.6% for U, 78.3% for S (V has only 16 IDs), so form type does not explain the disagreement.

Cohen's kappa corrects agreement for chance. It is 0.12 for the strict definition and 0.39 when e-scooters count. It is low even at 80.1% agreement because FLHSMV rates 90.6% of matched reports positive while the LLM rates 71.2%, and because the sample is built from two slices of the FLHSMV rating.

E-scooter cases are concentrated in a few agencies: Florida Highway Patrol (461), Miami Police Department (354), Broward County Sheriff's Office (221), Miami Beach PD (180), Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office (155). At Miami Police Department about 66% of FLHSMV-positive reports are E-scooter, yet its disagreement rate is only 6.6% because e-scooters count as a match there; under the strict definition it would look very different.

caveats: FLHSMV's rating is assigned by FLHSMV reviewers using the keyword criteria in the legend above, and the LLM is a model reading the narrative. Neither is treated as the final truth: where they disagree, this tab shows the disagreement and the likely reason, not a verdict.
FLHSMV's criteria use the narrative and the property-damage fields; the LLM was given only the narrative. Some disagreement is therefore about what each source was allowed to see.

Rule codes and their definitions come from the LLM's classification prompt. The LLM sometimes cites a code whose trigger wording does not appear in its own reasoning (see the last column of the rule table), so a code is a guide to why, not proof.
The 1,754 FLHSMV-positive reports the LLM called Other, and the 152 FLHSMV-positive reports it called Bicyclist without a property-field explanation, have not been hand-reviewed.
This tab is a fixed comparison on the matched sample and ignores the sidebar filters.
